podcasts.title: OpenAI’s Noam Brown: Why Game Theory Didn’t Lead to General Intelligence (Live at No Limit Finals)
podcasts.description: Noam Brown built the first AIs to beat top poker professionals, then concluded that game theory, the field his career was built on, was not the path to general intelligence. Recorded live at the Finals of No Limit, Sequoia’s pokerbot tournament, the OpenAI researcher describes his “crisis of faith”: game theory assumes everyone is rational, and the Diplomacy bots that won were the ones trained on human data to model how people actually behave in the messy real world. That sent him to OpenAI and the work that became o1, at a time when much of the field believed a bigger pre-trained model would solve everything. Noam explains why he asks every new model to build a pokerbot, where GPT-6 Astra still falls short, and why this is the “centaur period” of human plus AI. He argues that human progress has always been one giant recursive self-improvement loop, and shares his most controversial take: promising students should drop out and join the labs now. podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning
podcasts.title: Ep 98: China Expert on Jensen’s Return
podcasts.description: ChinaTalk host Jordan Schneider joins Jacob Effron on the day Jensen Huang returned as NVIDIA's CEO to talk about what the comeback means for the AI ecosystem and US-China competition, and why he thinks the political fight over AI is only getting started. Jordan has run ChinaTalk, the newsletter and podcast on technology, China, and US policy, for the past ten years, and this is his fifth emergency episode in a week and a half. Jordan and Jacob discuss the fact pattern behind Jensen's ouster, why Jordan sees NVIDIA's blind eye to chip smuggling as the real scandal rather than the spy allegations, why he thinks a falling stock market moved Trump more than Chinese access to chips, and whether NVIDIA and America's AI build-out are stronger with Jensen back at the helm. They also cover the new Commerce rule cutting off Chinese remote access through Malaysian data centers, why Jordan believes Mythos ended the argument that AI is a normal technology, what founders should expect as China starts putting export controls on its own data and models, why humanoid robots can still barely pick up a muffin and how much of robotics runs on Chinese rare earths, and why he thinks money can't solve the coming political backlash against AI. On Unsupervised Learning we probe the sharpest minds in AI in search for the truth about what's real today, what will be real in the future and what it all means for businesses and the world.
